problem: RL-based image-goal navigation encodes goal and observation images independently and fuses only their high-level semantic embeddings. Fine-grained goal details are lost, and the observation encoder cannot focus on goal-relevant regions.
motivation: Humans find a pictured place by comparing objects, shapes, colors and textures between the goal image and the current view. Existing policies lack this goal-conditioned perception, and map/memory-based methods need depth, GPS or pose sensors. The paper asks whether the goal image's fine-grained, high-resolution features can condition observation encoding directly.
key_idea: Use fine-grained, high-resolution goal-image features as prompts to condition observation encoding, either by channel-concatenating goal and observation at the pixel level (early fusion) or by FiLM-modulating early observation ResNet blocks with goal activation maps (mid fusion).
insight: Fusing the goal image at the pixel or feature-map level, rather than fusing final embeddings, gives a large gain (Table 3 ablation, 50M steps, SR: late fusion 13.0 -> mid fusion 77.3 -> early fusion 78.9). Fine-grained conditioning is essential: average-pooling the goal activations drops SR from 77.3 to 32.0, and self-attention instead of FiLM reaches only 13.9. Tied-weight encoders without joint input stay near baseline (14.6 vs 78.9), so goal-conditioning rather than weight sharing is the cause. Early layers matter most (fusing only ResBlock 1 is best). Early fusion is simplest, while mid fusion is more robust to mismatched goal-camera parameters (Table 8) and to instance-image goals (Table 9).
method: Early Fusion (FGPrompt-EF): concatenates goal and observation RGB along the channel axis (128x128x6) and feeds them to a single ResNet9/ResNet50 encoder, z_fusion = f_o(v_o ⊕ v_g).

Mid Fusion (FGPrompt-MF): the goal encoder's intermediate activation maps are mapped via 1x1 convs (plus an FC layer) to FiLM affine factors gamma and beta, which modulate the matching ResBlocks of the observation encoder. Fusing only the first block(s) works best.
Skip Fusion (FGPrompt-SF): a heuristic baseline that adds SuperPoint+SuperGlue matched keypoints (top-k coordinates, FC-embedded) to the concatenation z_g ⊕ z_o ⊕ FC(z_k).

Navigation policy: a 2-layer GRU (hidden size 128) takes z_fusion and the previous action and feeds an actor-critic, trained end-to-end with DD-PPO for 500M steps using the ZER reward (distance and angle shaping, slack 0.01, success reward requiring 1 m and 25° angle).
4-RGB panoramic variant: each of the four camera images is fused with the front goal image through the EF encoder and the outputs are concatenated.
Transfer to visual rearrangement: FGPrompt-EF fuses the unshuffled image with the current observation in a ResNet18 imitation-learning baseline.

setting.backbone: ResNet9 (main) / ResNet50 (EF variant) + 2-layer GRU actor-critic, trained from scratch with PPO
setting.model_size: ResNet9 encoder (FGPrompt-EF ~1/50 the parameter count of the SOTA OVRL-V2 per Fig. 1b); ResNet50 for one variant
setting.training_data: Gibson ImageNav episodes from Mezghani et al.: 72 train scenes x 9k episodes = 648k episodes, 500M steps, no pretraining or extra data. Ablations use 50M steps. Instance-ImageNav agents are trained on HM3D ImageNav.
setting.observation: egocentric RGB 128x128, 90° HFOV (single camera; 4-RGB panoramic variant in some comparisons)
setting.action_space: discrete low-level: MOVE_FORWARD 0.25 m, TURN_LEFT/RIGHT 30°, STOP
setting.simulator: Habitat (Gibson, MP3D, HM3D); AI2-THOR for rearrangement

results: FGPrompt-EF reaches 90.4% SR / 66.5 SPL on Gibson with ResNet9 and RGB only (92.3 / 68.5 with ResNet50), beating OVRL-V2 (82.0 SR / 58.7 SPL, ViT-B pretrained) with about 1/50 of the parameters. Trained only on Gibson, FGPrompt-MF transfers to MP3D (77.6 SR) and HM3D (76.1 SR), versus ZER's 14.6 and 9.6. In the 4-RGB setting it also beats memory-based TSGM (94.2 vs 81.1 SR).
limitations: Only validated in simulation; the authors say sim-to-real deployment is future work.
Instance-image navigation performance stays low (best SR 9.9%), and no memory or long-horizon exploration is used.
Early fusion is brittle when the goal camera parameters differ from the agent's, and mid fusion is more complex to design.
